messages.subject: Trouble processing Skyline data
parts:
Hi,

I'm using MSstats version 4.4.1
After loading the data, 
data <- SkylinetoMSstatsFormat(data)

I get
Error in setnames(x, value) :
  Can't assign 4 names to a 0 column data.table
Calls: do.call ... colnames<- -> names<- -> names<-.data.table -> setnames
In addition: Warning message:
In eval(jsub, SDenv, parent.frame()) : NAs introduced by coercion
Execution halted

The prior logs include : 
INFO  [2022-10-23 00:57:28] ** The following options are used:
  - Features will be defined by the columns: IsotopeLabelType, PeptideSequence, PrecursorCharge, FragmentIon, ProductCharge
  - Shared peptides will be removed.
  - Proteins with single feature will not be removed.
  - Features with less than 3 measurements across runs will be removed.

The issue seems to be similar to https://groups.google.com/g/msstats/c/BS7PRZ7g_ZA  but the suggestion provided there was to check features with combination of (protein name, peptide sequence, precursor charge).
The logs here seem to suggest features with more columns

Anyways, to verify this, I tried
  grouped_data <- data %>% group_by(BioReplicate,
                                    IsotopeLabelType,
                                    ProteinName,
                                    PeptideSequence, PrecursorCharge,
                                    FragmentIon, ProductCharge) %>% summarize(n = n())

and found that there are 'n' values in the range 1 to 6 (both inclusive)
So this seems to be something other than the filtering issue ?


I also ran this data on MSstats 3.18.5 (an older version in our high perf computing cluster)
SkylinetoMSstatsFormat executed fine
But trying to do 'dataProcess' on the output data, gives the error that multiple rows are present

messages.subject: Re: Trouble processing Skyline data
parts:
Thank you for your response, Mateusz.

Based on your hint, I tried replacing the full path of the file, in the filename column with just the filename (so as to avoid '/' character).
But that didn't make a difference 

Please find below link to modified version of subset of the data 
https://drive.google.com/file/d/17PYnx1xbcBc7hG1gElUn7QAgm7_HD6er/view?usp=sharing  

MSstats 4.4.1 as seen previously reported same error in SkylinetoMSstatsFormat step itself, MSstats 3.18.5 gave duplicates error in the 2nd step.
To resolve this I tried,

data <- SkylinetoMSstatsFormat(data)

data.processed <- data %>% group_by(BioReplicate, ProteinName,

slice_min(order_by = DetectionQValue, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup()

data_process_output <- dataProcess(data, logTrans = 2, normalization = FALSE, censoredInt = '0', remove50missing = FALSE)

This did work (only in MSstats 3.18.5), but I'm not really sure if I should be filtering like this based on Q-value.

Looking forward to your feedback :)
